root.name: Englund Gambit Declined: Reversed Mokele Mbembe

overview: Black declines to trade pawns on e5 and pushes 2...e4, and after 3.Ne5 the white knight lands centrally, attacked by ...d6 or ...Qg5. Black generally follows with ...d6, ...d5 and ...Nf6 to build a pawn chain on d5/e4 and challenge the knight, while White keeps a good space and tries to undermine e4 with f3 or Nc3. I do not recognise the name well, and read the position from its moves.

white_ideas.idea: Centralise the knight and challenge e4 with Nc3 or Bf4 and f3
Move the knight with Nc4 and play e3/Be2
Take control of the centre and aim for a small edge

black_ideas.idea: Play ...c6 and ...Qd5 or ...Bb4 to counter in the centre

typical_structures.structure: Black e4/d5 pawn chain against White d4

character.notes: Black's advanced e4 pawn creates tension but there is no forced attack; play is mostly positional and manoeuvring.

soundness.notes: Not clearly refuted, White probably has a slight edge.

structure.notes: e4 and d5 pawns lock the centre against d4, a closed-leaning structure; low confidence.

approach.notes: A rare Englund branch strong players hardly use.

character.reason: Neither side is under immediate pressure.

soundness.reason: White probably has a slight edge but Black is not refuted.

structure.reason: Black e4/d5 chain locks the centre against d4.

approach.reason: Englund family, rarely played by strong players.
